title: Konkan Guavas Fly to Gulf on Navi Mumbai Airport's First Export Cargo Flight
excerpt: Air India Cargo's inaugural international shipment from the new airport carried 1.79 tonnes of fresh produce to Abu Dhabi, opening a dedicated trade corridor for western India's agricultural exporters.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Air India Express's first international cargo flight carried 1.79 tonnes of produce to Abu Dhabi.
  • Navi Mumbai–Abu Dhabi service operates thrice weekly, with 2.5 tonnes cargo capacity per flight.
  • NMIA is set to become a major cargo hub as Mumbai's main airport suspends operations in 2026.
  • FedEx is building a ₹2,500-crore automated cargo hub at NMIA, creating over 6,000 jobs.
  • The new route enhances access to fresh produce for the Indian diaspora in the Gulf.
  • Air India Express flight IX207 carried 1,789 kg of Konkan guavas and drumstick moringa from Navi Mumbai International Airport to Abu Dhabi on July 15, marking the airport's first international cargo shipment.
  • The thrice-weekly Navi Mumbai–Abu Dhabi service offers about 2.5 tonnes of belly-hold cargo capacity per flight, with Air India Cargo projecting 25 tonnes of monthly export volume.
  • NMIA is poised to become a major cargo gateway as Mumbai's main airport suspends freighter operations for runway repairs starting August 2026, with FedEx, Cathay Cargo, Air France, and Lufthansa Cargo preparing to shift operations.

When Air India Express flight IX207 lifted off from Navi Mumbai International Airport (NMIA) bound for Abu Dhabi on July 15, its belly hold carried 1.79 tonnes of fresh guavas from Maharashtra's Konkan region and drumstick moringa — marking the airport's first international export cargo shipment and the formal launch of its international cargo services.

The consignment, modest in tonnage, signals the opening of a new agricultural trade corridor for western India. The Boeing 737 MAX 8 service, operated by Air India Express thrice a week, offers roughly 2.5 tonnes of belly-hold capacity per flight. Air India Cargo expects the route to move approximately 25 tonnes of export cargo each month.

"The first export shipment from Navi Mumbai connects growers, traders and businesses in western India directly with one of the region's most important international markets."

— Ramesh Mamidala, Head of Cargo, Air India

A New Gateway for Western India's Produce

For agricultural exporters in Maharashtra and neighbouring states, the Navi Mumbai–Abu Dhabi corridor reduces dependence on the congested cargo infrastructure at Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport (CSMIA) in Mumbai. The UAE remains one of India's largest markets for fresh fruits and vegetables, driven by rising demand for premium produce among health-conscious consumers across the Gulf.

> **"NMIA — a joint venture between Adani Airport Holdings Limited (AAHL) and the Maharashtra government's CIDCO — began domestic operations on December 25, 2025."**

Konkan guavas have long commanded strong demand in Gulf markets for their distinctive flavour, while drumstick moringa has emerged as a high-value export thanks to its growing popularity as a superfood. For Indian farmers, access to international buyers through reliable air cargo translates into significantly better price realisation than domestic markets can offer.

Air India Cargo's facilities at NMIA are GDP-certified — meeting globally accepted standards for handling temperature-sensitive shipments including fruits, vegetables, and pharmaceuticals. The cold chain infrastructure encompasses refrigerated trucks, temperature-controlled warehouses, specialised cargo containers, and thermal blankets designed to preserve freshness from farm to destination.

"Speed alone is not enough. Maintaining the integrity of the shipment from origin to destination is equally important."

— Ramesh Mamidala, Head of Cargo, Air India

NMIA's Rapid Rise as a Cargo Hub

The cargo milestone caps a swift ascent for India's newest greenfield airport. NMIA — a joint venture between Adani Airport Holdings Limited (AAHL) and the Maharashtra government's CIDCO — began domestic operations on December 25, 2025. In less than seven months, it has connected 46 domestic destinations, served over 2.3 million passengers, and now handles approximately 150 air traffic movements per day.

The airport's cargo ambitions extend well beyond belly-hold produce. In February 2026, FedEx broke ground on a ₹2,500-crore fully automated air cargo hub at NMIA — a 300,000-square-foot facility designed as a regional consolidation centre connecting India to Southeast Asia, West Asia, Europe, and the United States. The hub is expected to create more than 6,000 direct and indirect jobs.

NMIA's cargo role is set to expand further as Mumbai's main airport suspends dedicated freighter operations starting August 2026 for major runway, taxiway, and apron repairs expected to last until mid-2027. Cathay Cargo, Air France, and Lufthansa Cargo are already negotiating to temporarily relocate freighter services to NMIA, according to The Hindu Business Line.

What the Diaspora Should Watch

For the Indian diaspora in the Gulf, faster and more reliable air cargo from western India could mean fresher Indian produce — mangoes, guavas, drumsticks, and other perishables — reaching UAE and wider Gulf markets in better condition and at potentially lower logistics costs. The Navi Mumbai–Abu Dhabi route also strengthens passenger connectivity: Air India Express Chairman Nipun Aggarwal has described Navi Mumbai as a key pillar of the airline's dual-airport strategy alongside CSMIA.

What's Next

With its Terminal 2 being redesigned for a capacity of 50 million passengers annually and a long-term cargo handling target of 3.2 million metric tonnes per year, NMIA is positioning itself as western India's primary aviation and logistics gateway. As freighter operators migrate from Mumbai and new international routes open, the airport's first export shipment of Konkan guavas may come to mark the start of a significant shift in India's air cargo geography.
